t: You're standing on Frampton Street, in the City of Westminster. The street takes its name from Sir George Frampton, the British sculptor. He was a leading figure in the New Sculpture movement, mixing marble and bronze, with touches of Art Nouveau and Symbolism. He made many public monuments, including several statues of Queen Victoria and, after the First World War, a number of war memorials. Two of his best-known works are the Edith Cavell Memorial in London and the Peter Pan statue in Kensington Gardens.
